## Module Overview

### Module summary

caribou_SSUD maps caribou habitat use from an integrated step-selection analysis (iSSA).
It turns the model's fixed-effect coefficients into a steady-state utilization distribution [@PottsSchlagel2020]: the long-run density of use the model's habitat and movement terms imply over a landscape.
The result is a probability density of use (PDE) for each model, normalized to sum to 1 over the area it is predicted for, and a binned map of it (`pdeMap`) that compares the cells within that area.

The module has one code path for any caribou model: what differs between projects (the model, the landscape, layer names, defaults) is supplied as data or parameters.
The defaults are those of the northern mountain caribou (NMC) models fit with [`hsaCEtool`](https://github.com/JWTurn/hsaCEtool); a model made another way (e.g. a boreal caribou model fit within SpaDES) is mapped by setting the parameters to match how its model and layers were made (see "Matching a model" below).
The `ecotype` parameter is no longer used (it is ignored, with a message).
With `simulationScale` it maps the global model, one model per region, or both.

In static mode (`simulationProcess = "static"`, the default) it maps the baseline landscape only.
In dynamic mode it also rebuilds the landscape layers that change during a simulation every `predictionInterval` years from `predictStartYear`, and maps habitat use on each.
Each layer is matched by its name to what forecasts it (`dynamicLayers`), so layers should be named by one rule:

| Layer | Name | Forecast from |
|:--|:--|:--|
| forest cover | `prop_<type>_<res>`, e.g. `prop_forest_240` | the simulated tree cohorts (LandR) |
| time since fire | `ts_fire_<res>` | the simulated fires (e.g. `scfm`) |
| time since harvest | `ts_harv_<res>` | nothing yet: it only ages, as no module simulates harvest yet |
| distance to a feature | `dist_<feature>_<res>`, with `_adj` when capped, e.g. `dist_paved_240_adj` | the roads and mines `anthroDisturbance_Generator` adds, for the classes set in `disturbanceClasses` |
| amount of disturbance (not a distance) | starts with `disturb`, e.g. `disturb_prop_240` | not forecast |

`<res>` is the layer's resolution in m.
Every other layer (e.g. land cover other than forest) stays as in `modelLand`.
A layer coarser than the simulation's grid (e.g. a 1200 m layer on a 240 m grid) is built from the grid's cells, as the model's layers were.
The default patterns also match some older names without a resolution (e.g. `prop_needleleaf`, `timeSinceFire`, `distpaved`); such a layer is on the simulation's grid.

For a model fit with seasons (terms such as `seasonwinter:prop_forest_240_end`), the module makes a map for each season (`seasonMaps`) and a full-year map that combines them, weighted by season length or as chosen (`fullYear`, `seasonWeights`).

### Module inputs and parameters

The module needs the model and the landscape the model reads (Table \@ref(tab:moduleInputs-caribou-SSUD)):

- `iSSAmodels`, the models, named `global` and/or by region (e.g. `NT`). Each can be the fitted model (`glmmTMB`) or a table of its fixed-effect coefficients (columns `term` and `estimate`, as in hsaCEtool's `<model>_fixed.csv`), or a mix of the two.
  If not supplied, the global model's table is read from `<coefficientsModel>_fixed.csv` in the model's zip file, `<project>_model_<coefficientsModel>.zip`, in the Google Drive folder `modelsFolderID`; with `project = NA`, the models are read from `iSSAmodels.RData` in `outputFolderID` (for models not fit with hsaCEtool).
  (`iSSAcoefficients`, one table for the global model, still works but is deprecated.)
- For a model with seasons, `iSSAseasons`, the days in each season, used to weight the full-year map; read from the model's zip file when it has one.
- `modelLand`, the landscape layers, named as in the model's terms; a layer the model needs and the list lacks stops the run, naming it.
  If not supplied, the landscape the project's models were fit on is read from `model_land_<baselineYear>.tif` in `<project>_model_land_<baselineYear>.zip` in the Google Drive folder `landFolderID` (as hsaCEtool uploads it); with `project = NA`, from `modelLand.tif` in `outputFolderID`.
  The project name thus pairs each model with its landscape.
  Distances capped for the model (e.g. more than 20 km set to 21 km) carry `_adj` in their names (e.g. `dist_paved_240_adj`).
- `studyAreaCaribou`, the area the global model was fit on, and, for the regional models, `studyArea_juris`, one area per region.
  Optionally, `studyAreaReporting`, an area to normalize and bin the maps over instead (see `pdeArea`).
- Optionally, a baseline made earlier (`pde` and `pdeMap`, or a folder, zip file or URL in `baselineSource`), so the baseline is read rather than made again.

In dynamic mode it also uses, from the other modules of the simulation:

- the simulated forest (`cohortData` and `pixelGroupMap`, with `sppEquiv` to tell conifers from broadleaf species);
- the time since fire (`timeSinceFire`): only fires burned in the simulation (from `baselineYear` on) are read from it, so a map that starts from stand age is not read as fire history;
- the human disturbance (`disturbanceList`);
- the simulation's grid (`rasterToMatch`), which every `modelLand` layer must match. If the model
  has layers coarser than the grid's cells, the grid's top-left corner must also be a multiple of
  each of those resolutions. A template cropped to a study area should be snapped outward to the
  coarsest template resolution, not just the model's (e.g. 4800 m for templates up to 4800 m, even
  if the current models go up to 1200 m), so later models with coarser layers fit too.

A forecaster that is missing leaves its layers as they are: fire and harvest layers only age, and distances stay as in `modelLand`.

```{r moduleInputs-caribou-SSUD, echo = FALSE, eval = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
df_inputs <- SpaDES.core::moduleInputs("caribou_SSUD", "..")
knitr::kable(df_inputs,
             caption = "List of (ref:caribou-SSUD) input objects and their description.")
```

The parameters (Table \@ref(tab:moduleParams-caribou-SSUD)) choose the models and the area each is mapped over (`simulationScale`, `pdeArea`), static or dynamic mode and the prediction years (`simulationProcess`, `predictStartYear`, `predictionInterval`, `predictLastYear`), and where the model, its landscape and a premade baseline come from (`project`, `coefficientsModel`, `modelsFolderID`, `landFolderID`, `baselineSource`).

#### Matching a model

The module cannot tell how a model's layers were made, so the settings below must match it.
The defaults are those of the NMC models; a model made another way needs its own values.

| Setting | Set it to | Default (NMC models) |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `project`, `coefficientsModel` (or supply `iSSAmodels` and `modelLand`) | the hsaCEtool project and model to download; `project = NA` reads `iSSAmodels.RData` and `modelLand.tif` from `outputFolderID` (models not fit with hsaCEtool) | `"NMC"`, `"bioseason_fullV2_to2020"` |
| `simulationScale`, `jurisdiction` | which models to map: `"global"`, `"regional"` (one model per region, named as in `jurisdiction`, e.g. `"NT"`) or `"both"` | `"global"` |
| `rasterToMatch` (input) | the grid of `modelLand` (see above) | none |
| `baselineYear` | the year `modelLand` describes; the simulation should start in it | 2025 |
| `dynamicLayers` | a pattern on layer names for each source (forest, fire, harvest, disturbance) | the naming rule above, plus the older names |
| `forestTypes` | the LandR forest types each forest layer counts | `prop_forest`: all forest; `prop_needleleaf`: conifer; `prop_mixedforest`: deciduous and mixed |
| `movingWindow` | the circle each forest layer was averaged in: a pattern on layer names and a radius in m, e.g. `data.frame(layers = "^prop_", radius = 720)` | 240 m forest layers in 500 m |
| `ts_else`, `noEventYear` | how `modelLand` stores cells that never burned or were never harvested: a fixed number of years (`ts_else`), or years since a stand-in year (e.g. `noEventYear = list(fire = 1900, harvest = 1900)`) | 200 years |
| `fireCoarse`, `harvestCoarse` | the rule the model's layers coarser than the grid were built with: the mean (`"mean"`) or the most recent (`"recent"`) fire or harvest year of their cells | `"mean"` (the V2 models; the earlier ones used `"recent"`) |
| `disturbanceClasses` | the `anthroDisturbance_Generator` classes each distance layer is measured to; a distance with no class stays as in `modelLand` | the Yukon classes |
| `distanceCellSize`, `distanceCap` | the cell size distances were measured on, and the cap for `_adj` layers | 30 m; more than 20 km set to 21 km |

`forestForecast` chooses how forest layers are forecast: `"change"`, the default, adds the simulated change since the start to `modelLand`'s layer; `"LandR"` uses the simulated forest alone.
In `movingWindow`, a radius of `NA` takes the input `buffer`, the radius other modules in the workflow use (e.g. prepTracks); a different radius stops, so the modules cannot disagree.
Only forest layers take a window so far.

```{r moduleParams-caribou-SSUD, echo = FALSE, eval = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
df_params <- SpaDES.core::moduleParams("caribou_SSUD", "..")
knitr::kable(df_params, caption = "List of (ref:caribou-SSUD) parameters and their description.")
```

### Events

- `init`: makes the baseline PDE and map for the current landscape, or reads a premade one, and saves a baseline it made to the output folder.
  In dynamic mode it also schedules the two events below, from `predictStartYear` every `predictionInterval` years, and in the last year when `predictLastYear` is `TRUE`.
- `simLayers` (dynamic mode): rebuilds the layers that change, on top of the layers that do not (`fixedSSUD`), and writes the stack:
  - forest cover: the simulated cohorts classed into forest types, as a share of each cell at the layer's resolution (and of a circle around it, for layers `movingWindow` picks);
  - time since fire: the most recent of `modelLand`'s fire and the simulation's, in years; cells that never burned get `ts_else`, or keep counting from `noEventYear` when it is set;
  - time since harvest: `modelLand`'s, aged to the year;
  - distances: the smaller of `modelLand`'s distance and the distance to the simulated features of that class, so features outside the simulated area, or of classes the simulation does not add, still count; `_adj` layers are capped again. Distances with no class in `disturbanceClasses` stay as in `modelLand`.
- `calcSimPde` (dynamic mode): maps habitat use on the rebuilt layers with the same models as the baseline, into `simPde` and `simPdeMap`, and writes them.

### Plotting

The module does not plot.

### Saving

A baseline the module makes is written to `pde_<.studyAreaName>/` in the output folder, as `pde_<model>.tif` and, when `normalizePDE` is `TRUE`, `pdeMap_<model>.tif`; each file is registered as an output.
The model is `global` or a region (e.g. `pde_global.tif`, or `pde_NT.tif` for a regional model named `NT`).
For a model with seasons, a season's maps are named `<model>_<season>` (e.g. `pde_global_winter.tif`), and the full-year map as the model.
In dynamic mode, each prediction year's layers and maps go to its `sims/` subfolder, with the year in their names (e.g. `pde_global_year2030.tif`).

### Links to other modules

In dynamic mode, the simulated forest comes from the LandR Biomass modules ([`Biomass_borealDataPrep`](https://github.com/PredictiveEcology/Biomass_borealDataPrep), [`Biomass_core`](https://github.com/PredictiveEcology/Biomass_core): `cohortData` and `pixelGroupMap`; [`Biomass_regeneration`](https://github.com/PredictiveEcology/Biomass_regeneration)), and the time since fire from the fire model ([`scfm`](https://github.com/PredictiveEcology/scfm)'s `scfmSpread`: `timeSinceFire`).

The human disturbance comes from [`anthroDisturbance_Generator`](https://github.com/FOR-CAST/anthroDisturbance_Generator) (`disturbanceList`).

The model and its landscape can be made in one of two ways:

- outside SpaDES with [`hsaCEtool`](https://github.com/JWTurn/hsaCEtool), which fits the iSSA and uploads the model and its landscape layers (`modelLand`) by project (as for NMC);
- within SpaDES, by a chain of modules (as for some boreal projects): [`caribouLocPrep`](https://github.com/gc-rmcinnes/caribouLocPrep) (cleans the collar locations and makes the study areas, `studyAreaCaribou` and `studyArea_juris`), [`prepTracks`](https://github.com/gc-rmcinnes/prepTracks) (makes the steps), [`prepLandscape`](https://github.com/JWTurn/prepLandscape) (makes the yearly landscape layers), [`extractLand`](https://github.com/gc-rmcinnes/extractLand) (extracts the layers at the steps) and [`caribouiSSA`](https://github.com/gc-rmcinnes/caribouiSSA) (fits the `glmmTMB` models, `iSSAmodels`, and hands on the landscape they read, `modelLand`).
